A720NKOU3BRK1 refers to baseband version. Baseband is a firmware that controls the radio on your device. It is responsible for wireless communication between your device and the network.
It is bootloader version. Due to Samsung\'s security policy, you cannot downgrade from higher bootloader version firmware to lower bootloader version firmware.
A720SKSU3BRK1 refers to the build version. You can get the bootloader version, One UI version, firmware build year, month and the revision number(minor version) from the build version.
It is model number. In this case, A720 is Samsung Galaxy A7 (2017).

It is month when firmware was built.

A means January,
B means February,

L means December.

It is One UI version.
If yellow text is updated, it means One UI is going to be or has been updated.

A means very first major version.
B means major update has been released once.
C means major update has been released twice.

Z means beta firmware.
It is region code. In this case, SKS means South Korea. It could be 4-letter-code.

It is revision number (minor version).

1 means firmware was built once.

A means firmware was built 10 times.

It is year when firmware was built.

T means 2020,
U means 2021,
V means 2022, and so on.
A720SSKC3BRK1 refers to CSC version. CSC is an abbreviation for Consumer Software Customization and refers to the specific regional or carrier firmware installed on a Samsung device.

Firmware information consists of 3 information. They are build version, CSC version, and baseband version.

Suppose that firmware search result is
A720SKSU3BRK1/A720SSKC3BRK1/A720NKOU3BRK1.

First one(A720SKSU3BRK1) refers to build version,
second one(A720SSKC3BRK1) refers to CSC version,
last one(A720NKOU3BRK1) refers to baseband version.
